# AGENTS.md — TypeScript & Next.js Repository ## Build & Verification - Package manager: npm / pnpm (check lockfile before running). - Verify after final edits: `npm run typecheck && npm test`. ## Conventions - Prefer strict TypeScript types; avoid `any` assertions and silent catches. - Keep Server Components default; mark Client Components only at leaf interactive boundaries. - Reuse existing hooks, validation schemas, and design tokens before adding packages. ## Reporting - Summarize exact changed file paths, root cause, and observed test results only. Never claim checks passed without running them.

Download TypeScript / Next.js AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — Python & Data Pipeline Repository ## Environment & Checks - Use project virtual environment (`.venv/bin/python` or `uv run`). - Run `pytest` and `ruff check` before reporting completion. ## Engineering Rules - Handle missing or malformed records explicitly rather than silent drops. - Never hardcode credentials, tokens, or personal host paths in committed code; read from environment variables. - Document assumptions, data denominators, and schema contracts clearly.

Download Python AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — Monorepo Shared Workspace Safety ## Scope & Isolation - Check `git status` before and after edits; touch only the package directory requested. - Do not modify root lockfiles, CI workflows, or shared test harnesses unless explicitly authorized. - Keep every instruction section compact (stay well under Codex's 32 KiB limit). ## Verification - Run package-local build and tests after your final edit and report exact counts.

Download Monorepo AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — Autonomous PR Review Instructions ## Review Priority 1. Security vulnerabilities, auth/permission bypasses, injection vectors, and secret leaks. 2. Correctness bugs, state desync, race conditions, null/boundary failures, and broken contracts. 3. Missing test assertions or untested error paths. ## Output Rules - List blocking defects first with file + line reference and concrete reproduction path. - Omit cosmetic nitpicks unless they violate project linter rules. Never praise code before listing bugs.

sections.h2: Twelve more AGENTS.md templates by workflow.
sections.html:
5. Minimal Personal Global (~/.codex/AGENTS.md)

# Global Communication Preferences - Start responses with root cause, modified files, and test output; skip long preamble. - Read existing repository files completely before editing. - Ask before running destructive git commands, dropping tables, or adding dependencies. - Never fabricate test results or unverified tool output.

6. Go Microservice

# AGENTS.md — Go Service - Verify after edits: `go test -race ./... && go vet ./...`. - Wrap errors with context (`fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`); avoid `panic` outside startup. - Keep interfaces narrow at consumer sites; avoid global mutable state.

7. Rust Crate

# AGENTS.md — Rust Crate - Verify after edits: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`. - Avoid `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` in library code; propagate typed errors cleanly. - Keep `unsafe` blocks documented with explicit safety invariants.

8. Database & Migrations Guardrail

# AGENTS.md — Database Migrations - Never edit previously applied migration files; always generate a new forward migration. - Check locking risk on large tables (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, nullable column backfills). - Test both apply and rollback against local seed database before finishing.

9. Static Site & Web Accessibility

# AGENTS.md — Web Frontend - Use native semantic HTML (<button type="button">, <details>, proper <label for>) over div click handlers. - Enforce 44x44px touch targets and visible keyboard `:focus-visible` outlines. - Run build & link/HTML structure tests after every change.

10. Documentation & MDX Sync

# AGENTS.md — Documentation Repo - Check real source code / CLI `--help` output before documenting any flag or path. - Keep prose scannable and concrete; lead with exact runnable examples. - Never leave stale URLs or deprecated flags unflagged.

11. High-Speed Bug Triage Agent

# AGENTS.md — Bug Fix Mode - Write a failing reproduction test first, confirm the failure, then apply the minimal fix. - Report: (1) Root Cause in 1 sentence, (2) Minimal Diff, (3) Verified Test Output.

12. Test-Hardening Specialist

# AGENTS.md — Testing Focus - Do not mock core pure logic under test; mock only slow network/external I/O boundaries. - Never loosen failing assertions to make tests pass—fix the underlying bug or escalate cleanly.

13. Codex CLI AGENTS.override.md (Per-Directory)

# AGENTS.override.md - For files under this directory ONLY: skip end-to-end Docker builds during tight iteration; run `npm test -- --filter=unit` cleanly before handoff.

14. Security Audit Read-Only Agent

# AGENTS.md — Security Audit - Operate strictly read-only; do not modify production files unless explicitly instructed. - Check OWASP top vectors, auth bypasses, command injection, path traversal, and secret leaks. - Include exact line numbers and exploitable call paths for every finding.

15. Solo Founder Full-Stack Repo

# AGENTS.md — Ship Fast & Safely - Keep solutions boring and maintainable; prefer 1 clear helper over premature frameworks. - Verify full build compiles cleanly and key smoke tests pass before reporting done. - Alert immediately if missing `.env` secrets or external API changes block progress.

16. Multi-Agent Research & Evaluation Harness

# AGENTS.md — Research Repo - Never modify frozen raw datasets or benchmark ground-truth splits. - Record exact seed, model slug, temperature, and sample size N beside every result table.

faq.q: What is the 32 KiB limit on AGENTS.md in Codex?
faq.a: OpenAI Codex defaults project_doc_max_bytes to 32 KiB combined across global (~/.codex/AGENTS.md) and nested repository AGENTS.md / AGENTS.override.md files. Anything past 32 KiB gets silently truncated.

faq.q: Can I share one AGENTS.md across Cursor, Windsurf, and Copilot?
faq.a: Yes—many coding tools now read root AGENTS.md natively, or you can convert snippets cleanly between AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .cursor/rules/*.mdc with our Coding Rules Builder.
